BILL NUMBER:  S2830

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the canal law, in relation to the method of
abandonment for the purposes of the canal system


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This bill would make the method of abandonment for canal property more
open for discussion by the general public within that municipality or
locality to which a proposed sale of canal property is located.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Section one of this bill would amend Section 51 of the canal law, as
amended by chapter 335 of laws of 2001, to require abandonment notices
to be published in the newspaper in the county or the municipality or
locality wherein such lands are located when there is such a
newspaper. This amendment would also require that the corporation hold
a public hearing, at which evidence or further information may be
submitted, when it is the case that the assessment for such lands
proposed for abandonment is equal to or greater than fifty thousand
dollars. The current law says that the corporation  MAY  hold a public
hearing.  Section two provides for the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :
In large counties where there are more than one city, a person buying
an abandoned piece of property owned by the canal corporation may do
so without informing the citizens through a required public hearing in
which it will occur. Because the current law requires notices to be
published in a county newspaper, the person trying to buy the land
should publish their purchase notice in the city or town located in
that county if they have a local newspaper other than a county wide
newspaper. By requiring that the corporation shall hold a public
hearing, it invites interested parties to file oral or written
statements either supporting or opposing the proposed abandonment.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007-08: A.963 - Passed Assembly; Referred to Senate Transportation
Committee
2005-06: A.156 - Passed Assembly; Referred to Senate Transportation
Committee
2004: A.4642 - Passed Assembly; Referred to Senate Rules Committee
2003: A.4642 - Referred to Assembly Tourism, Arts and Sports
Development Committee.
2002: A.9939-A - Passed Assembly; died in Senate Rules Committee.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None to the state

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law.

summary: Provides that the New York state canal corporation shall cause to be published in a newspaper in the municipality or locality where such lands are located notice of such abandonment and shall after publishing notice hold a hearing at which evidence or further information may be submitted.
title: Relates to the method of abandonment for the purposes of the canal system
